subject: Order schedule: floor fallback + packaging compatibility — redlines
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@acerohealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acerohealth.com, contracts@wilsonhart.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order schedule: floor fallback language and package compatibility

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the order schedule and have two areas they want clearer language on before we proceed to signature:

1) Floor fallback: the current exhibit says a "floor" applies to committed token spend but is silent about what happens if usage migrates from Hosted API to Dedicated capacity mid-term (billing months 7–12). Our CFO wants an explicit fallback rule — e.g., whether the floor migrates pro rata to Dedicated pricing or remains applied to Hosted spend only.

2) Packaging compatibility: the packaging appendix lists SKU bundles A/B/C but the redline we received earlier drops the "compatibility" sentence that allowed temporary cross-use of adjacent bundles during migrations. We need an explicit migration grace so we don't face double-billing during a 30–day migration to Dedicated.

I've attached Acero's markup of the schedule (Acero_OrderSchedule_Redline_v3.docx) and an internal spreadsheet that maps expected monthly token splits. Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: (a) add a short fallback clause for floor treatment when switching capacity types, and (b) reintroduce a 30-day migration grace with a reconciliation true-up?

If you want, we can have Wilson & Hart prepare a short, clean mark to accept once Redwood confirms the commercial intent.

Best,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Director, Strategic Sourcing
AceroHealth

[Attachment: Acero_OrderSchedule_Redline_v3.docx] [Attachment: Acero_Monthly_Splits.xlsx]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhang <e.zhang@acerohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: floor fallback language and package compatibility

Emily —

Thanks for the clear callout and for the attached markups. We're aligned on the commercial intent and agree this should be explicit in the schedule. High-level responses below; I've attached our suggested draft language (Acero_OrderSchedule_Redline_v3.docx with Redwood comments) and a pricing matrix showing pro rata math for the fallback scenario. Key points:

• Floor fallback behavior: Redwood proposes the floor remains linked to the COMMITTED QUANTITY in the order schedule. If a Customer migrates usage from Hosted to Dedicated mid-term, the floor will be treated as an order-level commitment and allocated pro rata across resource types for billing purposes, with any differential credited/true-d up at the end of the relevant billing period. Concrete example included in the draft.

• Migration grace: We're willing to reintroduce a 30-day migration grace during which cross-use of adjacent bundles is permitted. During the grace period, invoices will not double-bill; instead, Redwood will invoice based on actual usage and apply the committed floor against aggregated usage. A reconciliation true-up will occur at the end of the 30-day window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik and Laura — can you review the two short clauses in the attached doc and confirm they pass legal/pricing? (I highlighted places we need firm language.)
2) If okay, we'll return a clean mark for Acero and ask Wilson & Hart to confirm.

Karthik: one specific pricing nuance — for pro rata allocation we assume token parity across Hosted and Dedicated (i.e., $/token base matches the order schedule). Ben, please confirm whether there are any platform fees tied to Dedicated that should be excluded from the floor math.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0147

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Emily Zhang <e.zhang@acerohealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: floor fallback language and package compatibility

Marissa / Emily —

Quick internal/legal check here. I reviewed the proposed clauses and redlines. High level: commercial approach is fine, but we should tighten the fallback definition to avoid ambiguity around "pro rata" allocation and the treatment of Dedicated-only platform surcharges. Proposed edits below (apologies for the compact style):

1) Define "Fallback Allocation" as "an allocation of the committed floor amount across billing resource types based on actual usage volumes during the billing period, expressed as a percentage of total billable units (e.g., tokens)." This prevents parties from trying to allocate by $ amount vs. unit count.

2) Exclude any Dedicated-only infra surcharge (listed in the Pricing Matrix as 'Dedicated Platform Fee') from the floor allocation; the floor should apply to core token/feature usage only. Dedicated-only surcharges will be billed and settled separately and will not reduce the committed floor amount.

3) For the 30-day migration grace, add a sentence requiring both parties to provide usage logs within five (5) business days of the grace-period end to enable reconciliation. That keeps the true-up timing bounded for finance teams.

If that sounds OK Emily, I'll convert these bullets into a short legal paragraph and attach a clean mark. Laura — if you want to flag anything else from a legal/regulatory perspective (e.g., data residency effects on Dedicated pricing), please flag now.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

(on behalf of Redwood Legal)

To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule: floor fallback language and package compatibility

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and for the clear examples. The approach looks reasonable to us. A couple of small asks from Acero: (a) please ensure the example math is included in the final exhibit so our finance team can follow the pro rata calculation line by line, and (b) we would prefer the Dedicated Platform Fee to be visible in the Pricing Matrix (as a separately invoiced line) rather than buried in notes.

If you can convert Karthik's bullets into the short legal paragraph and send a clean mark, Wilson & Hart will do a fast confirm and we can move to countersignature.

Emily
Emily Zhang
Director, Strategic Sourcing
AceroHealth
